topic: Advanced Use of Storage Classes and Linkage for Modular Programming
explanation: In advanced C programming, understanding and leveraging storage classes (auto, static, extern, register) and linkage specifications is crucial for controlling variable scope, lifetime, and visibility across multiple translation units. Proper use of these features enables sophisticated module design, encapsulation, and optimization techniques, especially when managing complex systems or libraries. Mastery of storage classes also helps avoid common pitfalls like symbol conflicts and undefined behaviors related to variable linkage.
keywords: C storage classes, C linkage, extern static, modular C scope
